summary: Pacifica sits on a narrow coastal shelf between the Pacific Ocean and the western slopes of Montara Mountain, which means fog rolls in most summer evenings and burns off by mid-morning — the data confirms it, with an average daily high of just 63°F year-round, making it one of the coolest incorporated cities in the Bay Area even on days when San Jose hits 90. That geography also means the town is essentially a string of neighborhoods threaded along Highway 1 and Pedro Point, separated by steep hillsides and creek valleys rather than connected by a grid, so driving between the north and south ends can feel longer than the city's 12.6 square miles suggest. The coast here is dramatic — sheer bluffs, surfable breaks, and direct trail access to the Golden Gate National Recreation Area — but the employment picture is essentially a bedroom-community story, with most workers commuting north into San Francisco or south toward Silicon Valley. At a median household income of roughly $157K against a median home price above $1.2 million, the price-to-income ratio sits near 7.7, which means even at the local median income a conventional purchase requires substantial savings or existing equity. Rent at $3,080 absorbs about 24% of that median gross income, a more manageable ratio, which partly explains why the city's housing stock skews toward rentals in its denser corridors. Pacifica is the rare Bay Area address where you can surf before work and still be at a desk in SoMa within 30 minutes — but the trade-off is a thin local retail and dining scene that reflects a town of 37,000, not the urban variety just over the hill.
